newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Congress approves Car Industry Regime.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Congress approves Car Industry Regime.

text.p: Brazil's Congress Thursday approved decrees setting up car industry rules that favour manufacturers with Brazilian factories and establish fiscal incentives for investment in the Northeast, officials said.
A Congress official said the two presidential decrees, both being contested by Brazil's trading partners, were approved in a joint session of the lower and upper houses.
One of the decrees sets a preferential 31 percent tariff for cars imported by domestic manufacturers, while those with no domestic production base face a stiff 62 percent tax.
The tariffs were 35 percent and 70 percent last year, respectively, but were reduced this year in accordance with World Trade Organization rules which call for gradual cuts in import tariffs.
Brazil is currently holding talks with the United States at the WTO on the tariff rules, which have already resulted in some $20 billion in pledged investment from major global car makers.
The other decree, issued by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in December, is an attempt to encourage car makers to build plants in the impoverished Northeast states.
It has been sharply criticized by Argentina, which fears it will lose out in the battle for investment.
Under Brazilian rules, the president can issue 30-day decrees which have the power of law. The decrees can be reissued indefinitely until they are voted on by Congress.
Deputy Jose Carlos Aleluia, who presented the decrees to Congress for a vote, said only one item had been altered in the decree governing fiscal incentives for the Northeast.
According to the private Invest News agency, the deadline for companies to take advantage of the incentives, which include long-term tax breaks, was extended to May 31 from March 31.
